rationales.1: Seasonal shelf sections, a month filter, and bold price plus color-coded stock in fixed card positions make every packet legible at a glance on both widths.
rationales.2: Price bottom-left, stock bottom-right, a plain Add to basket with quantity on the product page, and conventional stock wording keep the money path entirely unclever; the only quibble is that just one card shows an explicit view link.
rationales.3: Out of stock is red and plain, the null-price sweet pea says Price on request with no invented figure, the estimated germination is labeled, and the UK-only banner sits above the fold on both surfaces.
rationales.4: Large serif headings, roomy cards, generous buttons, and no hover-dependent information hold up at mobile width with full content parity.
rationales.5: The cream, brick, and green palette, packet-frame illustration motif, and consistent card rhythm read as one system across catalog, product page, and both color modes.
rationales.6: The sowing table, potting-shed note, difficulty line, and companion cards with price and stock let a first-timer decide on the page.
rationales.7: The rack by the shop door is a one-sentence idea a two-person shop would truly own, and shelves, packet-shaped cards, and copy all reinforce it.
rationales.8: Novelty stays in the shelf metaphor and botanical icons while navigation, filtering, and purchase mechanics remain fully conventional.
rationales.9: Lines like two of us keep it stocked and for the patient gardener are warm and specific, though a shade less individual than the strongest rival.
rationales.10: A repeat visitor scans shelf headers, green and red stock states, and the only-nine-left flag immediately, and the two surfaces cohere as one shop.

rationales.1: The single-file numbered list is legible but slow: prices sit inline rather than in a scannable column, and season fit hides in small meta lines with no seasonal grouping.
rationales.2: The product page commerce box is fully conventional, but the catalog offers no visible route into most packets and asks the shopper to read rather than act.
rationales.3: Estimated germination is flagged, the sweet pea says price pending rather than inventing a number, and out of stock is plain, though the UK-only line is a small centered footnote.
rationales.4: Type is generous and nothing depends on hover, but the delicate serif meta text and centered layout give older tablet readers more work than the grid rivals.
rationales.5: The hairline rules, numbered entries, and restrained typography are genuinely refined and carry identically into dark mode and mobile.
rationales.6: The product page covers sowing table, growing note, difficulty, and companions cleanly, so a first-timer can decide without leaving.
rationales.7: The kept ledger idea suits two growers who vouch for every line, though it leans literary-editorial more than service culture.
rationales.8: All novelty lives in the numbered-list voice and typography while every commerce mechanic stays conventional.
rationales.9: Read slowly, choose well is a sentence no competitor would publish, and the tone holds across both surfaces.
rationales.10: A returning shopper must walk the whole flat list to find what is in season or back in stock, which is exactly the visit this design serves worst.

rationales.1: Desktop rows with right-aligned prices and seasonal drawers scan beautifully, but on mobile the carrot and sweet pea entries collapse into a one-word-per-line column that destroys glanceability.
rationales.2: Mechanics are recognizable, yet the inline quantity steppers on catalog rows add mild cleverness to the money path and the controls are unusually small for commerce.
rationales.3: This is the most honest surface of the four: the out-of-stock line explains the new harvest is being cleaned and tested, the pending price promises a note when it is set, and the footer discloses the germination method.
rationales.4: The tiny minus, plus, and Add targets fall below comfortable tablet sizes for older readers, and the broken narrow-column wrap on mobile compounds the problem.
rationales.5: Desktop rhythm and the restrained green palette are handsome, but the mobile column collapse and the floating price-pending note breaking the row grid mean the two surfaces do not hold as one system.
rationales.6: The product page is the best of the panel, with an at-a-glance stat trio in plain language, a reassuring growing note, and companion links that give reasons.
rationales.7: The potting bench with seasonal drawers is congruent with two growers who vouch for every packet, and the copy keeps the metaphor honest.
rationales.8: Voice and drawer metaphor stay in the brand layer, but the stepper-in-catalog choice edges novelty toward checkout-adjacent mechanics.
rationales.9: The easiest drawer on the bench and do not be discouraged by the quiet first month are the most ownable sentences on the panel.
rationales.10: Seasonal drawers, filter chips, and restock promises serve a repeat visitor well on desktop, but the mobile rendering failure undercuts the return trip.

rationales.1: The twelve-segment month bar under every packet shows season fit instantly, with aligned price and stock lines and a sidebar month filter backed by section links.
rationales.2: Purchase mechanics are entirely conventional on the product page, and the bars stay informational rather than touching the money path.
rationales.3: The estimated germination gets both a label and a margin note explaining it, the null price stays honest as price pending, scarcity is stated plainly, and UK-only shipping leads both pages.
rationales.4: Type is generous, margin notes are always visible rather than hover-revealed, and the bars are redundantly backed by bold sow-month text, though the unlabeled segments ask a little inference.
rationales.5: The almanac structure, marginalia column, and disciplined green-and-plum palette carry consistently across surfaces, widths, and modes.
rationales.6: The year bar plus table, difficulty line, margin quote, and companion entries give a first-timer everything needed to commit on the page.
rationales.7: Find your month first, then your packet is a one-sentence idea expressed in structure, visualization, copy, and filtering alike, and it is true of a shop organized around sowing windows.
rationales.8: The month-bar and marginalia novelty lives entirely in the brand and information layer while navigation and purchase stay conventional.
rationales.9: Shelved under the window it wants and the margin asides are specific and unhurried, just short of the strongest voice on the panel.
rationales.10: A repeat visitor asking what can I sow now is served faster here than anywhere else, and the bar motif ties catalog and product page into one shop.
